title: Quarterly Retail E-Commerce Sales — Q3 2026 (the quarter that LOST Prime Day, not the one that settles it), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: CENSUS: three independent census.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research, all naming the date. (1) retail/release_schedule.html (HTTP 200, 52,397 bytes), the Retail Indicator Branch's own schedule, whose "Quarterly Retail E-Commerce Report" table reads "3rd Quarter 2026 | November 19, 2026" under the column header "Release Date at 10:00 am". (2) CB26-133, the Q2 2026 release ITSELF (retail/mrts/www/data/pdf/ec_current.pdf, HTTP 200, 451,087 bytes, published 2026-08-18), whose page-1 closing line reads verbatim: "The Quarterly Retail E-Commerce sales estimate for the third quarter of 2026 is scheduled for release on November 19, 2026 at 10:00 A.M. EST." (3) retail/mrts/www/E-Creleasedates.xls (HTTP 200, 33,792 bytes, an OLE2 workbook authored by the Retail Indicators Branch, Last Revised March 19, 2026), whose "Third Quarter Data" column reads 19 on the 2026 row, in the November block. The three are independently maintained artifacts — a schedule page, a press release, and a historical-dates workbook — and they agree on both date and clock, including EST rather than EDT (2026-11-19 falls after DST ends 2026-11-01). Promoted estimate -> confirmed and EST: -> CENSUS: on the two-primary precedent this calendar carries for advance-services-q3-2026-11-19, housing-starts-2026-12-17, m3-full-report-2026-12-03 and durable-goods-2026-11-25; three were read here. ONE HONEST QUALIFIER RECORDED RATHER THAN BURIED: this report is ABSENT from census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html — all 179 rows of the 2026 Principal Federal Economic Indicators calendar were parsed 2026-09-09 and contain zero e-commerce entries, while listing advance-services-q3-2026-11-19 at the same 10:00 slot. It is a supplemental Census release, not a PFEI, which is a real difference from its 11-19 sibling and part of why impact is low. Confirmed is a claim about the SCHEDULED DATE, not about publication risk; the lapse history is in the ledger. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-09) after reading its one proposal, `from-retail-sales-2026-09-16`, which is now shadowed. The proposal's DATE work stands and was extended from one primary to three. Its ANALYTIC premise does not, and the refutation comes from the report's own published data. (1) THE PROPOSAL HAD THE PRIME-DAY SIGN INVERTED. It argued Q3 2026 is the quarter whose reference window "CONTAINS the Prime-Day shift on both sides" and is therefore "the quarterly settlement of the monthly argument." Amazon moved Prime Day 2026 to June 23-26 (aboutamazon.com, sourced by the sibling ledgers retail-sales-2026-10-15 and -11-17). June is Q2. So Q2 2026 GAINED the event and Q3 2026 LOST it, with no fall Amazon event announced for 2026 to offset in-quarter. Q3 is the payback quarter, not the settlement quarter, and its y/y also faces a hard base because Q3 2025 did carry a July Prime Day. (2) THE ONE PRIOR JULY->JUNE MOVE PRODUCED NO DETECTABLE QUARTERLY FINGERPRINT. 2021 is the only other year Prime Day left July for June. Measured from Census's own tsadjustedsales.xlsx (107 quarters, Q4 1999 -> Q2 2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09): Q3 2021 e-commerce SA q/q was -1.6%, the only negative Q3 in the 2015+ window — but Q2 2021, the quarter that GAINED the event and should have been flattered, posted the WORST relative growth of that entire year (e-commerce q/q minus total q/q: Q1 -0.9, Q2 -2.3, Q3 -0.3, Q4 +0.4). The reopening rotation dominated both quarters and the Prime-Day term is not separable from it. A 92-day aggregate cannot attribute a 4-day event. (3) THE REPORT DOES NOT MEASURE THE LINE THE PROPOSAL THINKS IT ISOLATES. Per CB26-133's own Survey Description, e-commerce is collected across ALL retailers — "Coverage includes all retailers whether or not they are engaged in e-commerce" — so it spans store-based online sales and is not NAICS 454 nonstore; and its "total retail sales" denominator is a sample of "approximately 10,800 retail firms EXCLUDING food services," so it is not the monthly headline's denominator either. Two overlapping aggregates, not one line item. (4) THE +12.2% Y/Y THE PROPOSAL LEANED ON OVERSTATES THE TREND. On a two-year stack the same series annualizes to 8.54% (Q2 2024 $288,822M -> Q2 2026 $340,244M), against 7.92% for Q2 2024 and 6.04% for Q2 2025 — real acceleration, roughly 3.7pp smaller than the headline y/y, which is flattered by a soft 2025 base and the pulled-in June event. Impact LOW and symbols empty on measured grounds: 0 mentions of e-commerce across 1,871 GDPNow vintages (ContribArchives, 2014-05-01 -> 2026-07-28, fetched direct 2026-09-09); the Atlanta Fed's forward PostedUpdates calendar posts vintages on 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-18 but NONE on 2026-11-19; 0 macro- or commerce-keyed hits in trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md (re-grepped 2026-09-09); not a Principal Federal Economic Indicator; and the whole Q3 monthly nonstore series is already public by 11-19. Date confirmed; nothing here licenses an entry.
